name: Avia
_turns: How many turns a game lasts (the arena doc); the turn track at the table's end has a slot for each.
_grid: One character per tile, row 0 = the far side (player 2), last row = player 1's side. Each character is defined in the legend. From a photo of the user's drawn board (mapstomake/avia.webp; mapstomake/avia.png is the same photo with the user's colour notes: red/blue outlines round the land, yellow = a high ground tile, light blue = a low ground tile, green = the platforms' starts, purple = where the corner jump pads land (not painted: the user had the rings removed); taken from player 2's side: turned 180 degrees and perspective-straightened), 17 by 17, the same turned round (the spawns swap): all the land at one height (the user: only the marked tiles are high or low): a stone cross (each player's two spawn islands and the centre, joined by one-tile strips) and four grassy islands in the corners (a flag each), sky between them with 16 floating platforms, and jump pads; one high ground tile on each grassy island's arm, a low ground tile in each strip and under the centre flag.
_legend: level = height step: the land is level 1, high ground tiles (H) level 2, low ground tiles (_, and the centre flag F) level 0; tiles interact only within 1 level. The high and low tiles are sloped (the user), inside their own tile so the land round them stays flat (slant 0.559: 60 degrees, as on Snow and Yaksha): a high tile slopes down to the land on every side; a low tile rises up to the land beside it (rise: true, as Pugilis's pit onto its stairs; sheer: true = its drop to the sky stays a wall). surface picks the look from the palette (stone on the cross, grass on the corner islands). ~ = sky (no board); x / o = sky where a floating platform starts / where its track ends (see platforms). Jump pads (double chevrons, never turned: they point the way they throw): ^ v > < on the grass, U D R L on the stone (up/down/right/left as seen by player 1). G = a flag on a grassy island, F the centre flag (low ground).
_marker_style: plain: the spawns (an S with the player's number as a subscript, as drawn) and the jump pads' double chevrons are painted as bare translucent white symbols (the user's choice, like the buttons' icons), no rings or colours. The spawns have orient: out: their bottom toward the board's nearest edge, read from outside their island, as on the drawing.
_platforms: Floating platforms (3D pieces, tools/place_pieces.py): each starts on the first tile of its path (an x on the drawing) level with the land (platform_level), and its button glides it along the L to the last tile and back again (Global.lua), carrying the Pokemon on it.
_float: Floating islands like Illusio's: the whole board is lifted this many world units (at tile 3.24875) above the table (1.932: the land, level 1, tops out where Illusio's level 0 does, ~3.3 above the table), island edges drop a short cliff below the land (rim_level 1: as thin as Illusio's islands; a low tile at the edge drops it below its own top), and below that the rock tapers down to points (steps: its underside on a grid 3 x finer than the tiles, not 4: twice Illusio's land, so fewer vertices).
_board: The published board files the map picker uses (from tools/build_board.py; update when a new version is published), then run tools/build_arena_index.py.
_mountains: The islands are mountaintops (the user), each its own mountain: no underside; from the foot of each island's cliffs a rough rock face runs down and out at this slope (3.73: 75 degrees) to the table, a cover of clouds; steep enough that the mountains stay apart over the gaps between the islands. The board's outer edge drops straight to the table.
_table: Image for the table around the board (placeholder until the arena gets its own).
_textures: Placeholders from tools/draw_placeholders.py: mossy stone bricks on the cross (the user's pick over pale flagstones; not flipped, so the rows run the same way on every tile), windswept grass on the corner islands, pale layered rock on the cliffs and undersides.
